It converts clients’ communication into accessible formats, which required writing custom code and hand-fixing mistakes. Doctors found a tumor in Tony’s brain when he was a teen, which caused degenerative sight loss. When he was registered blind in his thirties, he struggled to adapt and mostly gave up on being active. Decades later, though, a friend invited him to train for a 5k and did not give up until Tony agreed. “I never imagined I could run with limited vision. But with the support of people around me, I can do this,” Tony says. He now advocates for other people who are blind or partially sighted to try a sport, including through the Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB). He says, "Just because we can’t see or can’t see fully, doesn’t mean we can’t do. We've just got to believe in ourselves, and magic will happen.”
